name: Seated Shoulder Extension Stretch
summary: A seated floor stretch that targets the anterior deltoids, pectorals, and biceps by sliding the hips away from hands placed behind the body.

setup: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat on the ground.
Place your palms flat on the floor behind you roughly shoulder-width apart, with your fingers pointing away from or slightly turned out from your body.
steps: Keep your arms straight and your chest lifted upward.
Slowly scoot your hips and feet forward away from your hands until you feel a gentle stretch across the front of your shoulders and chest.
Hold the position steadily without bouncing, breathing deeply.
Gently slide your hips back toward your hands to release the stretch.
instructions.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly, using long exhales to allow the front of the shoulders to relax deeper into the stretch.
cues: Do not shrug toward the ears

common_faults.fault: Excessively rounding the thoracic spine and letting the shoulders dump forward.
common_faults.correction: Keep the sternum lifted and gently retract the shoulder blades.

common_faults.fault: Bending the elbows significantly, reducing tension on the shoulder extensors and biceps.
common_faults.correction: Keep the arms straight throughout the hold without hyperextending the joints.

precautions: Stop immediately if you feel sharp anterior shoulder pain or impingement rather than a muscular stretch.
